## Loading

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| error: false

library(tidyverse)
library(easystats)
library(brms)
library(rstan)
library(patchwork)
library(ggside)
library(ggdist)

restore_units <- function(df, illusion = NULL) {
  if(!is.null(illusion)) df$Illusion_Type <- illusion
  df <- df |> 
    mutate(
      # Inverse of fit_model.R's normalisation. Difference is on [-1, 1] with 0
      # at the per-illusion mid-point difficulty (2026-09-20); a fit made before
      # that is on [0, 1] and cannot be read with this function. The bounds are
      # the observed per-illusion min/max of abs(Illusion_Difference) -- the
      # Ebbinghaus min (0.05, not 0.07) and the VerticalHorizontal max (0.30,
      # not 0.24) were wrong until 2026-09-20.
      Illusion_Difference = case_when(
        Illusion_Type == "MullerLyer" ~ (Illusion_DifferenceZ + 1) / 2 * (0.46 - 0.04) + 0.04,
        Illusion_Type == "Ebbinghaus" ~ (Illusion_DifferenceZ + 1) / 2 * (0.70 - 0.05) + 0.05,
        Illusion_Type == "VerticalHorizontal" ~ (Illusion_DifferenceZ + 1) / 2 * (0.30 - 0.03) + 0.03,
        .default = NA
      ),
      Illusion_Strength = case_when(
        Illusion_Type == "MullerLyer" ~ Illusion_StrengthZ * 49,
        Illusion_Type == "Ebbinghaus" ~ Illusion_StrengthZ * 2.03,
        Illusion_Type == "VerticalHorizontal" ~ Illusion_StrengthZ * 66.50,
        .default = NA
      )
  )
}
```

## Computational Cost

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5

# Sampling efficiency: bulk effective sample size per second of sampling wall
# clock, computed chain by chain so that the spread across chains is visible.
# Only the population-level parameters are counted (the smooth coefficients,
# their SDs and the group-level SDs): the thousands of participant offsets would
# otherwise dominate the average and say more about the data than the sampler.
data_efficiency <- function(m, pars = "^b_|^bs_|^sd_|^sds_") {
  draws <- posterior::as_draws_array(m, variable = pars, regex = TRUE)
  # Time per chain. Efficiency is per second of *sampling*, the usual
  # convention, but what one actually waits for is warmup + sampling, so both
  # are kept. This is wall clock, so it is only comparable between fits of the
  # same data with the same number of threads per chain - hence those are
  # carried along too and printed under the plot.
  time <- rstan::get_elapsed_time(m$fit)
  threads <- as.numeric(m$fit@stan_args[[1]]$num_threads)

  purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(posterior::nchains(draws)), function(chain) {
    # Parameters that were fixed rather than estimated (sigmadrift = 0 and the
    # like) have no effective sample size, hence the na.rm
    ess <- posterior::summarise_draws(
      posterior::subset_draws(draws, chain = chain),
      ess_bulk = posterior::ess_bulk
    )$ess_bulk
    data.frame(
      Chain = chain,
      ESS = mean(ess, na.rm = TRUE),
      Time_warmup = time[[chain, "warmup"]],
      Time_sample = time[[chain, "sample"]],
      Time_total = time[[chain, "warmup"]] + time[[chain, "sample"]],
      ESS_per_sec = mean(ess, na.rm = TRUE) / time[[chain, "sample"]],
      Threads = if (length(threads) == 1) threads else NA_real_,
      N = stats::nobs(m)
    )
  })
}

efficiency <- purrr::imap_dfr(models, \(m, name) mutate(data_efficiency(m), Model = name)) |>
  mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = names(models)))

# Model-level summary: the chains of a model average to one point
efficiency_means <- efficiency |>
  summarise(.by = Model,
            ESS_per_sec = mean(ESS_per_sec),
            Time_total = mean(Time_total))

# What each fit was: two models are only comparable here if these match
caption <- efficiency |>
  summarise(.by = Model,
            label = sprintf("%s: %d chains, %g threads/chain, n = %s",
                            first(Model), n(), first(Threads),
                            format(first(N), big.mark = ","))) |>
  pull(label) |>
  paste(collapse = "\n")

efficiency |>
  ggplot(aes(x = ESS_per_sec, y = Time_total / 3600, colour = Model)) +
  # One point per chain, and the model's mean on top of them
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.35) +
  geom_point(data = efficiency_means, size = 5, shape = 18) +
  # Both axes log: families differ in cost per gradient by orders of magnitude
  # (the DDM's numerical quadrature is 55x, see cogmod_ddm_cost_issue.md), and
  # on a linear axis the cheap ones collapse onto the origin
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Effective sample size per second of sampling (bulk ESS / s, log)",
    y = "Wall clock per chain, warmup included (hours, log)",
    title = "Computational cost",
    subtitle = "One point per chain, diamond is the model's mean. Bottom right is cheap and efficient.",
    caption = caption
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = "grey40"))
```

## Posterior Predictive Check


```{r}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

plot_ppc <- function(models, observed = NULL, ndraws = 500, n_trials = 10000,
                     rt_range = c(0, 2.5), binwidth = 0.02, n_points = 512,
                     model_colors = c("#1E88E5", "#212121", "#FB8C00", "#6D4C41")) {

  if (is.null(names(models))) names(models) <- paste("Model", seq_along(models))

  # All models are checked against the same trials, passed in explicitly
  if (is.null(observed)) observed <- insight::get_data(models[[1]])

  # The predicted curve is the predictive RT distribution marginal over trials,
  # estimated by simulation. A random subset of trials estimates the same
  # distribution as all of them - each trial contributes ndraws simulated RTs
  # either way - so there is no reason to predict 320,000 trials x 50 draws
  # (16 million RTs per model, minutes per model) to draw a density curve that
  # 250,000 RTs already pin down. The histogram still uses every observed trial.
  pred_obs <- if (nrow(observed) > n_trials) {
    observed[sample.int(nrow(observed), n_trials), , drop = FALSE]
  } else {
    observed
  }

  # Defective densities: each response's curve is scaled by its own rate, so the
  # two areas sum to 1 and correct/error are directly comparable across models
  defective_density <- function(rt, response) {
    keep <- is.finite(rt) & is.finite(response)
    rt <- rt[keep]
    response <- response[keep]
    purrr::map_dfr(c(0, 1), function(r) {
      x <- rt[response == r]
      if (length(x) < 2) return(NULL)
      d <- density(x, from = rt_range[1], to = rt_range[2], n = n_points)
      data.frame(
        Response = factor(r, levels = c(0, 1)),
        x = d$x,
        y = d$y * (length(x) / length(rt)) * if (r == 0) 1 else -1
      )
    })
  }

  # Observed: histogram, put on the same defective-density scale
  obs_data <- observed |>
    mutate(bin = floor(RT / binwidth)) |>
    count(Error, bin, name = "n") |>
    mutate(
      x = (bin + 0.5) * binwidth,
      y = n / (nrow(observed) * binwidth) * if_else(Error == 0, 1, -1),
      Response = factor(Error, levels = c(0, 1))
    ) |>
    filter(x <= max(rt_range))

  # Predicted. brms::posterior_predict() calls the family's sampler once per
  # trial (thousands of calls of a few dozen draws each), and most of that is
  # fixed cost. cogmod's posterior_predict_<family>() methods take a vector of
  # observations, so the same draws come out of ~50 vectorised calls instead,
  # about 3x faster for the DDM - see ?posterior_predict_cogmod_ddm.
  predict_chunked <- function(m, newdata, ndraws, chunk = 50) {
    prep <- brms::prepare_predictions(m, newdata = newdata, ndraws = ndraws,
                                      allow_new_levels = TRUE)
    for (dp in names(prep$dpars)) prep$dpars[[dp]] <- brms::get_dpar(prep, dp)
    method <- get(paste0("posterior_predict_", m$family$name),
                  envir = asNamespace("cogmod"))
    chunks <- split(seq_len(prep$nobs), ceiling(seq_len(prep$nobs) / chunk))
    do.call(rbind, lapply(chunks, method, prep = prep))   # (draws * N) x 2
  }
  pred_data <- purrr::imap_dfr(models, function(m, nm) {
    pp <- predict_chunked(m, pred_obs, ndraws)
    rt   <- pp[, 1]
    resp <- pp[, 2]
    stopifnot(all(resp %in% c(0, 1)))
    defective_density(rt, resp) |> mutate(Model = nm)
  })
  pred_data$Model <- factor(pred_data$Model, levels = names(models))

  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_col(
      data = obs_data,
      aes(fill = Response),
      width = binwidth, alpha = 0.4
    ) +
    geom_line(
      data = pred_data,
      aes(color = Model, group = interaction(Model, Response)),
      linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.9
    ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("0" = "#43A047", "1" = "#F44336"),
      labels = c("0" = "Correct", "1" = "Error")
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = setNames(model_colors[seq_along(models)], names(models))) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = abs) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = rt_range) +
    labs(x = "RT", y = "Density", fill = "Observed", color = "Predicted") +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 0.6))) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

plot_ppc(
  models,
  observed = insight::get_data(models[[1]]),
  ndraws = 500
)
```

## Parameter Curves

### Compute Predictions

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7

# Display names for the parameters, in the order they are plotted. Names are
# the family's own ("mu", "ndt", ...), values are what goes in the panel
# titles. Several parameters mean different things from one family to the next
# - "mu" is a drift rate in the DDM and the log-mean of the correct response in
# the LNR, and "sigmabias" is the variability of the starting point in the DDM
# but its maximum (A) in the racing models - so the map is built per model.
param_labels <- function(gam) {
  lvls <- c("Error Rate" = "Error Rate",
            "Mean RT" = "Mean RT",
            "mu" = "mu",
            "nuone" = "Nu (Errors)",
            "driftone" = "Drift (Errors)",
            "sigmadrift" = "Drift Variability",
            "sigmazero" = "Sigma (Correct)",
            "sigmaone" = "Sigma (Errors)",
            "boundary" = "Boundary",
            "bias" = "Bias",
            "sigmabias" = "Bias Variability",
            "ndt" = "NDT",
            "sigmandt" = "NDT Variability")
  switch(
    insight::get_family(gam)$name,
    "cogmod_ddm" = {
      lvls["mu"] <- "Drift"
    },
    "cogmod_lnr" = {
      lvls[c("mu", "sigmazero", "sigmaone")] <-
        c("Nu (Correct)", "Nu Variability (Correct)", "Nu Variability (Errors)")
    },
    # Both racing families: mu is the drift of the accumulator for correct
    # responses and driftone that of the other one, and sigmabias is the
    # start-point range A rather than a variability around a bias
    "cogmod_rdm" = {
      lvls[c("mu", "sigmabias")] <- c("Drift (Correct)", "Start Point Range")
    },
    "cogmod_lba2" = {
      lvls[c("mu", "sigmabias", "sigmazero", "sigmaone")] <-
        c("Drift (Correct)", "Start Point Range",
          "Drift SD (Correct)", "Drift SD (Errors)")
    }
  )
  lvls
}

# Rename the parameters and put them in canonical order. Parameter_Order keeps
# that order recoverable once the models are stacked together, where the factor
# levels of families that do not share their parameters get merged in whatever
# order the models happen to come in.
format_parameters <- function(pred, gam) {
  lvls <- param_labels(gam)
  found <- unique(as.character(pred$Parameter))
  # A parameter the map does not know about (a family added later) keeps its
  # own name and goes last, rather than silently becoming an NA panel
  unknown <- setdiff(found, names(lvls))
  if (length(unknown) > 0) lvls <- c(lvls, setNames(unknown, unknown))
  lvls <- lvls[names(lvls) %in% found]

  pred$Parameter_Order <- match(as.character(pred$Parameter), names(lvls))
  pred$Parameter <- factor(unname(lvls[as.character(pred$Parameter)]),
                           levels = unname(lvls))
  pred
}

# Predictions for each of the model's own parameters (mu and the auxiliaries,
# minus the outlier weight) over whatever grid is passed. The curves and the
# heatmaps below differ only in that grid, so they share this.
predict_parameters <- function(gam, datagrid) {
  params <- insight::find_auxiliary(gam)
  params <- c("mu", params[!params %in% c("poutlier")])
  purrr::map_dfr(params, function(p) {
    estimate_relation(gam, data = datagrid, predict = p) |>
      mutate(Parameter = p)
  })
}

# Parameters against illusion strength, one curve per illusion difficulty
data_curves <- function(gam) {
  datagrid <- insight::get_datagrid(gam, length = c(Illusion_DifferenceZ = 5, Illusion_StrengthZ = 30))
  pred <- estimate_prediction(gam, data = datagrid, centrality = "mean",
                              # TODO: increase iterations
                              iterations = 500, keep_iterations = TRUE) |>
    mutate(Parameter = Component, Type = "GAM") |>
    select(-Component, -Row) |>
    mutate(Parameter = ifelse(Parameter == "response", "Error Rate", "Mean RT"))

  # Only keep iterations of correct responses to compute mean
  iters_rt <- data.frame(select(pred[pred$Parameter == "Mean RT", ], starts_with("iter_")))
  iters_rt[data.frame(select(pred[pred$Parameter == "Error Rate", ], starts_with("iter_"))) == 1] <- NA
  pred[pred$Parameter == "Mean RT", "Predicted"] <- rowMeans(iters_rt, na.rm = TRUE)
  # Remove mean RTs when only a few correct trials as it's noisy
  pred[pred$Parameter == "Mean RT", "Predicted"][pred[pred$Parameter == "Error Rate", "Predicted"] > 0.9] <- NA
  pred <- select(pred, -starts_with("iter_"))

  # Add the predictions for the parameters of the model itself
  pred <- rbind(pred, mutate(predict_parameters(gam, datagrid), Type = "GAM"))

  pred |>
    format_parameters(gam) |>
    # Restore the original scale of the illusion strength and difference
    restore_units(illusion = "MullerLyer")
}

# Stack the models. Adding one to `models` in the loading chunk is all it takes
# for it to get its own column in every plot below.
preds_curves <- purrr::imap_dfr(models, \(m, name) mutate(data_curves(m), Model = name)) |>
  mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = names(models)))
```



### Visualize

```{r}
# Column header
make_header <- function(label) {
  ggplot() +
    annotate(
      "text",
      x = 0, y = 0,
      label = label,
      fontface = "bold",
      size = 5
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1, 1), ylim = c(-1, 1)) +
    theme_void()
}

# One column per model, one row per parameter, with panel(model, parameter)
# drawing each cell. The models do not share their parameters, so rows cannot
# be matched by name: each model's parameters are packed from the top in
# canonical order (which lines up the drift rates and the nus, both "mu"), and
# the non-decision time - the one parameter every family has - is anchored to
# the bottom row. Models with fewer parameters get spacers in between, so the
# columns stay aligned however many parameters they have.
plot_parameter_grid <- function(data, panel,
                                anchor_bottom = c("NDT", "NDT Variability"),
                                header_height = 0.35) {
  data$Model <- droplevels(factor(data$Model))
  model_names <- levels(data$Model)

  slots <- lapply(model_names, function(model) {
    d <- data[data$Model == model, ]
    params <- unique(as.character(d$Parameter[order(d$Parameter_Order)]))
    list(top = params[!params %in% anchor_bottom],
         bottom = params[params %in% anchor_bottom])
  })
  n_top <- max(lengths(lapply(slots, `[[`, "top")))
  n_bottom <- max(lengths(lapply(slots, `[[`, "bottom")))

  columns <- Map(function(model, s) {
    rows <- c(s$top, rep(NA_character_, n_top - length(s$top)),
              rep(NA_character_, n_bottom - length(s$bottom)), s$bottom)
    panels <- lapply(rows, function(p) if (is.na(p)) plot_spacer() else panel(model, p))
    wrap_plots(c(list(make_header(model)), panels), ncol = 1,
               heights = c(header_height, rep(1, length(rows))))
  }, model_names, slots)

  wrap_plots(columns, nrow = 1)
}

# Prepare data
curves <- preds_curves |>
  filter(!Parameter %in% c("Error Rate", "Mean RT")) |>
  mutate(Illusion_Difference = factor(Illusion_Difference))

# Colour scale
curve_cols <- colorRampPalette(
  c("#FF5722", "#FFC107", "#8BC34A", "#4CAF50")
)(nlevels(curves$Illusion_Difference))

# Function for individual panels
make_curve <- function(model, parameter) {
  ggplot(
    filter(curves, Model == model, Parameter == parameter),
    aes(Illusion_Strength, Predicted, colour = Illusion_Difference)
  ) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1.3) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = curve_cols) +
    labs(title = parameter) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        hjust = 0.5,
        size = 11,
        margin = margin(b = 4)
      ),
      axis.title = element_blank()
    )
}

plot_parameter_grid(curves, make_curve) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(
    legend.position = "right",
    plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 4, 4)
  )
```

## Parameter Heatmaps

### Compute Predictions

```{r}
# The same parameters as the curves, but over the full 2-D grid of illusion
# strength x illusion difference rather than five difficulty levels
data_heatmaps <- function(gam, n = 40) {
  datagrid <- insight::get_datagrid(gam, by = list(Illusion_DifferenceZ = seq(-1, 1, length.out = n),
                                                   Illusion_StrengthZ = seq(-1, 1, length.out = n)))
  predict_parameters(gam, datagrid) |>
    format_parameters(gam) |>
    restore_units(illusion = "MullerLyer")
}

preds_heatmaps <- purrr::imap_dfr(models, \(m, name) mutate(data_heatmaps(m), Model = name)) |>
  mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = names(models)))
```

### Visualize

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 12

# Function for individual panels
make_heatmap <- function(model, parameter) {
  ggplot(
    filter(preds_heatmaps, Model == model, Parameter == parameter),
    aes(x = Illusion_Strength, y = Illusion_Difference)
  ) +
    geom_tile(aes(fill = Predicted)) +
    geom_contour(aes(z = Predicted), color = "white", alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.5, bins = 20) +
    # The region of the space that might be psychometrically optimal
    annotate("rect", xmin = -30, xmax = 30, ymin = 0.1, ymax = 0.4,
             fill = NA, color = "red", linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "turbo") +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(title = parameter, fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11, margin = margin(b = 4)),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      legend.key.width = grid::unit(0.25, "cm"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 7)
    )
}

# Each parameter is on its own scale, so unlike the curves the fill guides
# cannot be collected: every panel keeps its own colour bar
plot_parameter_grid(preds_heatmaps, make_heatmap) &
  theme(plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 4, 4))
```
